dct_description_sm: Availability of drinking water is a major issue for northern communities in Quebec and throughout Canada. Given the presence of permafrost, these communities are mainly supplied by surface water which can be of poor quality and remains vulnerable to freezing during winter. More recently, global warming is leading to thawing of permafrost in the north, which is gradually increasing groundwater supplies. Using groundwater as a new source of drinking water could help solve many water supply issues. Numerical models have already been developed to simulate groundwater flow in cold regions, but few are based on field experiments. The main goal of this project is to improve numerical models that simulate the complex dynamics of groundwater flow and permafrost evolution, based on heat transfer and groundwater data collected on two permafrost mounds (BS and SB) located in a small watershed near Umiujaq.
dct_title_s: Heat and water balances of two permafrost mounds in Umiujaq, Nunavik, Qubec
